title: Dividing a quantity in a ratio
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:55Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank's sharing cards are the same method but are broader, covering simplifying ratios and unit conversion too, and their questions test those other skills, so none fits this Year 7 sharing point cleanly.

draft.title: Dividing a quantity in a ratio
card: To share an amount in a ratio, work in three steps: add the parts, find one part, then multiply.
Step 1: add the parts of the ratio to get the total number of parts. For 2:3, there are 2 + 3 = 5 parts.
Step 2: divide the amount by the total parts to find one part. For $60, one part is $60 ÷ 5 = $12.
Step 3: multiply one part by each number in the ratio. 2 × $12 = $24 and 3 × $12 = $36. Check: $24 + $36 = $60.
draft.remember: Add the parts, divide to find one part, then multiply.

a.q: $40 is shared in the ratio 1:3. What is the larger share?
a.why: There are 1 + 3 = 4 parts, so one part is $40 ÷ 4 = $10. The larger share is 3 × $10 = $30. The answer $10 is the smaller share, not the larger one.
a.clue: Add the parts first, then divide $40 by the total.

b.q: Priya and Sam run a stall and share a $350 profit in the ratio 3:4. How much more does Sam get than Priya?
b.why: There are 3 + 4 = 7 parts, so one part is $350 ÷ 7 = $50. Priya gets $150 and Sam gets $200, so Sam gets $50 more. The amount $200 is tempting, but it is Sam's share, not the difference.
